meta.method: Built the universe from ZoomInfo search_companies (private, 12-250 employees, PA/NJ/MD/DE) using radius passes around Lancaster (17601; 50 and 100 mi), Carlisle (17013), Chambersburg (17201) and Toms River (08753; 50 mi), plus the Authority Brands One Hour, Benjamin Franklin and Mister Sparky location directories, parsed for every PA/NJ/MD/DE territory. Each candidate's ownership, founding year, trades and on-site review counts were checked against its own website (fetched pages listed in sources) and, for franchisees, search-indexed BBB, LinkedIn, chamber and franchisor pages. PE- or strategic-owned operators were moved to pe_backed_competitors using PrivSource, sponsor press releases and roll-up trackers. Fit score (0-100) is five 20-point components: density_adjacency (distance to the Lancaster/Harrisburg/York or Beachwood nodes and whether the target is in a core county), trade_mix (HVAC+plumbing+electrical scores highest), scale (25-150 employees ideal), ownership_readiness (multi-decade founder/family ownership scores higher; ESOP or anti-PE messaging scores lower) and brand_alignment (Authority Brands franchisees score 20; ex-franchisees and review leaders next).

scoring_rubric.density_adjacency: 0-20; 18-20 = inside a core county or <=30 mi from a PP node; 13-17 = 30-60 mi; 8-12 = 60-120 mi; <8 = beyond screen
scoring_rubric.trade_mix: 0-20; 20 = HVAC+plumbing+electrical; 15-16 = two trades (+IAQ/water); 11 = single trade; minus 3-5 for fuel/commercial-heavy
scoring_rubric.ownership_readiness: 0-20; 14-17 = founder or multi-generation family with long tenure; 10-13 = mid-tenure owners/unknown; <=7 = ESOP, recent relaunch or explicit anti-PE stance
scoring_rubric.brand_alignment: 0-20; 20 = Authority Brands franchisee; 15 = former franchisee or 1,000+ reviews and rebrand-ready; 12-14 = 500+ reviews; 8-11 = other independents

fields: industries (fuzzy: hvac -> 0, plumb -> 0, construction, consumer services, repair)

ZoomInfo enrich_companies was unavailable (subscription limit), so employees and revenue_est_usd are ZoomInfo search-level modeled estimates and some are inconsistent (e.g., Warner, Timothy Off, Harris). Treat revenue as directional.

The web-search budget ran out mid-screen; ownership for several independents (Maitz, Central Penn, Good Inc, Lenegan) rests on the company's own site, with no independent PE-ownership check. Run a PitchBook/Grata check before outreach.
The PA Home Improvement Contractor registry was not queried in this run.
Distances are straight-line miles between city centroids (road miles are ~15-25% higher). Lat/lon are city centroids (geo_precision = city).

Authority Brands franchise owners are from search-indexed BBB, LinkedIn, chamber and franchisor pages; several owners are unverified (null). Harrisburg and York tri-brand locations are attributed to Punctual Pros by shared address and footprint, not by a filing.
The Pleasantville NJ tri-brand franchise trades as 'The Punctual Pros' and PitchBook conflates it with BSP's Punctual Pros. Confirm it is independent before any approach.
Oliver Heating & Cooling and Harris sit at or above the 250-employee edge and are closer to platform-scale mergers than tuck-ins.
Smith + Howard is excluded (BSP exit to TPG Growth, closed Aug 6 2026); this dataset covers Punctual Pros only.

items.company: Benjamin Franklin Plumbing / One Hour Heating & Air / Mister Sparky of West Chester (Ron Williams group)
items.ownership_notes: Search-indexed profile names Ron Williams as owner/founder (May 2002). Same owner is reported for One Hour / Benjamin Franklin of Delmarva (Berlin MD). West Chester runs all three Authority brands from 1313 Wilmington Pike.
items.brands_or_franchise: Benjamin Franklin Plumbing + One Hour Heating & Air + Mister Sparky franchisee (tri-brand)
items.review_source: Yelp listing shows 22 reviews for BF West Chester (Sep 2026 search result); Google count not retrieved
items.strategic_rationale: This is the closest tri-brand Authority territory to the Lancaster hub that Punctual Pros doesn't own. It fills Chester County (Main Line/Delaware Valley), the gap between Lancaster and Philadelphia. It uses the same brands, call-center scripts and pricebook, so it's a pure tuck-in with no rebrand. The owner also holds Delmarva (Berlin MD), so one negotiation could deliver two territories.
risk_flags: Owner has held the franchise since 2002 (succession angle, but valuation expectations may be anchored)
Headcount/revenue not disclosed; ZoomInfo has no clean record

items.company: One Hour Heating & Air / Benjamin Franklin Plumbing of Delmarva (Ron Williams group)
items.ownership_notes: Search-indexed chamber listing (Worcester County Chamber) names Ron Williams as owner of One Hour + Benjamin Franklin Delmarva, 9928 Old Ocean City Blvd, Berlin MD.
items.brands_or_franchise: One Hour Heating & Air + Benjamin Franklin Plumbing franchisee (Delmarva)
items.strategic_rationale: Comes with the West Chester deal (same owner) and adds the Ocean City/Delmarva shore market, which has seasonal second-home demand much like Horvath's Ocean County base. It's remote from Lancaster, so on its own it's an opportunistic add rather than a density play.
risk_flags: ~132 mi from Lancaster (125 mi from Toms River); outside the 120-mi screen radius (included only as a package with West Chester)

items.company: One Hour Heating & Air Conditioning / Benjamin Franklin Plumbing of Wilmington & Dover (Calvert's)
items.ownership_notes: Founded 1991 by Chris Lenhard as Calvert Heating & Cooling; David Murray partnered in 1995 (VP). Later adopted the One Hour mantle. Benjamin Franklin Wilmington operates from the same 410 Meco Drive address. BF/One Hour Dover (4282 N Dupont Hwy) uses a shared template; common ownership unconfirmed.
items.brands_or_franchise: One Hour Heating & Air + Benjamin Franklin Plumbing franchisee
items.strategic_rationale: A founder-owned dual-brand Authority franchise with 30+ years of history, covering northern Delaware (New Castle County) and possibly Dover. It's a tuck-in with no rebrand, links the West Chester corridor to Delmarva, and Mister Sparky is whitespace in the territory (Mister Sparky New Castle County is a separate franchise).
risk_flags: Founder-era leadership (1991), so a succession/transition plan is needed

items.company: One Hour Heating & Air of Bucks County / Benjamin Franklin Plumbing of Levittown & Doylestown
items.ownership_notes: Search-indexed BBB profile lists Michelle Glasson as President of Benjamin Franklin Plumbing - Levittown. One Hour Bucks County, BF Levittown and BF Doylestown all list 5503 (Bristol) Emilie Rd, Levittown.
items.brands_or_franchise: One Hour + Benjamin Franklin Plumbing franchisee (3 territories)
items.review_source: Yelp shows 30 reviews for BF Levittown (search result, Sep 2026)
items.strategic_rationale: Three Authority territories (Lower Bucks, Doylestown, Bucks HVAC) about 36 miles from Horvath's Toms River-area hub across the Delaware, bridging Horvath (Ocean/Monmouth) and Central PA. Mister Sparky BuxMont (Warminster) and Ardmore/Levittown (Jenkintown) are separate franchises nearby, so a three-way combination is possible.
risk_flags: Philadelphia suburbs are heavily contested by Sila (King of Prussia) and Horizon Services

items.strategic_rationale: A small northern Lancaster County (Denver/Reinholds) plumbing and HVAC shop near the Berks line. It fills the gap between Lancaster and Reading along US-222.
risk_flags: Younger founder-owners (2007) may not be sellers yet

items.revenue_source: ZoomInfo search_companies modeled estimate (retrieved 2026-09-24) (includes heating-fuel delivery)
items.ownership_notes: Family owned and operated since 1928; fuel delivery, HVAC and master plumber services.
items.strategic_rationale: A 98-year-old Harrisburg name with about 93 employees. Its fuel-oil customer base is a captive funnel for heat-pump conversions, which One Hour could harvest, and the HVAC/plumbing service business overlaps Punctual Pros' Dauphin/Cumberland territories. The fuel division could be carved out or divested.
risk_flags: Heating-fuel distribution revenue is non-core (carve-out needed)

items.company: Pronto Plumbing Heating Air & Drains (incl. former SECCO Home Services)
items.revenue_source: ZoomInfo search_companies modeled estimate (retrieved 2026-09-24) (sum of Pronto Plumbing 29 emp/$6.22M and SECCO Home Services 23 emp/$4.16M records)
items.ownership_notes: Serving Harrisburg/York/Lancaster since 1969. The site says 'The same trusted team from SECCO Home Services... now proudly serving homeowners as Pronto Plumbing Heating Air & Drains', indicating an owner-led consolidation of the two brands.
items.strategic_rationale: Already a two-brand consolidator on the West Shore with about 52 combined employees. It has a drains/water-quality specialty (the Benjamin Franklin upsell) and a Harrisburg/York/Lancaster service map identical to Punctual Pros' core.
risk_flags: Integration of the SECCO rebrand still in progress

items.company: WM Buffington Company Heating, Cooling & Plumbing
items.ownership_notes: Family-owned since 1952; David (President/Co-Owner) and Megan (VP/Co-Owner).
items.strategic_rationale: A small tuck-in about 4 miles from the Punctual Pros Harrisburg office (Patriot Rd). Its customer list would convert directly into One Hour/Benjamin Franklin routes around Steelton, Middletown and Hershey.
risk_flags: Small; value is mostly the customer list

items.ownership_notes: Founded 1989 by the Stambaughs; ownership passed to Christy & Mike Spangler in 2014. Two-time Bryant Dealer of the Year.
items.strategic_rationale: Adds route density to Punctual Pros' York node (Eastern Blvd) in western York County. Its Bryant-dealer HVAC install capability complements One Hour replacement sales.
risk_flags: Owners acquired in 2014, so a mid-tenure exit horizon

items.ownership_notes: Small family-owned business in business since 1998; three service technicians per the About page.
items.strategic_rationale: Covers southeastern York County (Red Lion/Dallastown) with geothermal and mini-split capability. It's a low-complexity One Hour tuck-in near the York office.
risk_flags: Small technician bench (3 service techs cited)

items.ownership_notes: Locally and family-owned, serving South Central PA since 2002.
items.strategic_rationale: A 41-person HVAC operator in York city. It would double One Hour York's technician capacity and adds residential plus light-commercial accounts.

items.ownership_notes: Local HVAC, plumbing and electrical company since 1958; residential focus.
items.strategic_rationale: A three-trade residential shop (including whole-house generators) in York, which maps directly onto One Hour, Benjamin Franklin and Mister Sparky. It adds electrical technicians, the scarcest trade in the Punctual Pros tri-brand model.
risk_flags: Thin web presence; review volume unknown

items.company: Rodney B. Smith Plumbing, Heating & Cooling, Inc.
items.ownership_notes: Established 1983 (40+ years).
items.strategic_rationale: The largest residential plumbing/HVAC independent screened in Franklin County (a Punctual Pros core county with no dedicated node). It could anchor a Chambersburg satellite along I-81.
risk_flags: ~72 mi from Lancaster; would need a satellite branch

items.ownership_notes: Since 2008; Matt McCleary, President.
items.strategic_rationale: A Franklin County HVAC add-on that could be paired with Rodney B. Smith to build a Chambersburg hub.

items.ownership_notes: Locally owned, family-run since 1986; Brad Mann, President. Has a commercial HVAC department.
items.strategic_rationale: Covers Franklin and Adams counties (between Chambersburg and Gettysburg). It adds plumbing capacity for a western satellite.

items.ownership_notes: Serving Shippensburg and south-central PA since 1976.
items.strategic_rationale: A 50-year-old western Cumberland County HVAC shop along the I-81 corridor that would bridge Harrisburg and Chambersburg.
risk_flags: Excludes mobile homes and tenant-requested service (narrower residential scope)

items.ownership_notes: Founded 2000 by Alan Rimmer (Owner/President); has a project superintendent, so some construction exposure.
items.strategic_rationale: A West Shore HVAC/plumbing tuck-in with a founder-owner. Its service department would fold into Harrisburg One Hour and Benjamin Franklin.

items.ownership_notes: Working in the community since 1972; serves Camp Hill and Carlisle.
items.strategic_rationale: A 54-year-old Cumberland County HVAC service base that would add routes to Harrisburg One Hour.

items.ownership_notes: Family owned and operated for more than eight decades; residential and commercial.
items.strategic_rationale: A multi-generation family shop in southern Franklin County (I-81/Hagerstown corridor). It's a bolt-on to a future Chambersburg hub.

items.ownership_notes: Family-owned and operated since 1992; fuel supplier expanded into heating, cooling, plumbing and generators; serves Berks, Lebanon and Dauphin.
items.strategic_rationale: A Lebanon County foothold (a core Punctual Pros county). Its fuel customer base can be converted to heat pumps and service agreements, and a carve-out of the home-services book is possible.

items.ownership_notes: Local family-owned company serving Berks County.
items.strategic_rationale: Berks County is a Punctual Pros core county with no dedicated node. This is a small Reading plumbing/HVAC entry point, now that P1 Service Group owns Essig Plumbing.

items.ownership_notes: Fifth-generation family-owned business serving Kutztown since 1906.
items.strategic_rationale: A 120-year-old northern Berks brand (Kutztown/Lehigh border) with water-quality capability. It's a stepping stone toward the Lehigh Valley.
risk_flags: Fifth generation newly active (2019), so they may intend to continue

items.ownership_notes: Employee-owned via ESOP: a large share of stock is held by 100+ full-time employee-owners across nine Aero locations; the remaining portion is owned equally by two rural electric cooperatives (Choptank Electric Cooperative, Denton MD; Adams Electric Cooperative, Gettysburg PA).
items.strategic_rationale: Adams/York County energy company with an HVAC service arm and a 35,000+ customer base. A carve-out of the HVAC service book (not the fuel business) could seed Adams County coverage.
risk_flags: ESOP plus rural electric cooperative (Choptank, Adams Electric) ownership

items.revenue_source: ZoomInfo search_companies modeled estimate (retrieved 2026-09-24) (site: 230+ employees, 145+ technicians, 160+ trucks)
items.ownership_notes: Founded 1971 by Joe Oliver; son David is the 2nd-generation owner (brother Bill is foreman of the sheet metal shop, John works part-time in the warehouse per the About page). Serves PA, NJ and DE.
items.brands_or_franchise: Independent (rebrand candidate or run as second platform brand)
items.strategic_rationale: A transformational, platform-scale deal: 230+ employees and 160+ trucks across the Philadelphia suburbs, South Jersey and Delaware. It would roughly triple Punctual Pros' headcount and connect the Central PA and Jersey Shore footprints, and its second-generation family ownership is outside PE today.
risk_flags: Size near the top of the 250-employee screen; needs larger equity check
Philadelphia suburbs are Sila and Horizon home turf (competitive auction likely)

items.company: Good Plumbing, Heating & Air Conditioning, Inc. (Good Inc.)
items.ownership_notes: Serving southeastern PA with mechanical services since 1949.
items.strategic_rationale: A scale plumbing/HVAC operator (~98 employees) in upper Montgomery County. Paired with One Hour Lansdale, it would build an eastern PA hub between Lancaster and Bucks.
risk_flags: Commercial mechanical exposure likely at this size

items.ownership_notes: Serving Allentown and the Lehigh Valley since 1964. The site has no PE disclosure; ownership was not verified in this run.
items.strategic_rationale: A three-trade Lehigh Valley brand that complements Benjamin Franklin Bethlehem. It would give Punctual Pros a Lehigh Valley node alongside HomeX (Deluxe Plumbing) and Sila-held competitors.

items.ownership_notes: Family-owned; plumbing, HVAC and electrical in the Lehigh Valley since 1988.
items.strategic_rationale: A three-trade Lehigh Valley tuck-in whose trade mix mirrors the tri-brand. It could be combined with Benjamin Franklin Bethlehem and Maitz.

items.company: Timothy Off Plumbing, Heating & Air Conditioning
items.revenue_source: ZoomInfo search_companies modeled estimate (retrieved 2026-09-24) (ZoomInfo also shows 74 employees; the pair is internally inconsistent)
items.ownership_notes: Locally owned and operated plumbing and HVAC company in West Chester for over 20 years.
items.strategic_rationale: A Chester County plumbing/HVAC tuck-in that could be combined with the West Chester Authority franchise to densify the Route 202/West Chester Pike market.
risk_flags: Sila (AQM Exton, Oxford Plumbing) and Northwinds (Horn Plumbing) are active acquirers in Chester County

items.ownership_notes: Family-owned since 1946. Joined One Hour in 2004 and started Mister Sparky in 2007 (per its company timeline); Urie Boulden Jr. sold to Tim & Michael Boulden in 2007; renamed Boulden Brothers in 2013; sold its propane division in 2019.
items.brands_or_franchise: Independent (former One Hour / Mister Sparky franchisee)
items.strategic_rationale: A 96-person, four-trade New Castle County operator that already ran the One Hour and Mister Sparky playbooks. Re-entry into the Authority system (or a dual-brand approach) would be culturally easy, and with Calvert's One Hour it would give Punctual Pros northern Delaware leadership.
risk_flags: Left the franchise system by 2013, so re-franchising may be resisted
Horizon Services (New Mountain) is headquartered in the same market

items.revenue_source: ZoomInfo search_companies modeled estimate (retrieved 2026-09-24) (revenue appears understated relative to headcount)
items.ownership_notes: Third generation of family ownership since 1937; 4.8 stars on Google (count not shown).
items.strategic_rationale: A third-generation family business with ~108 employees in Frederick. It opens the I-270/Frederick market south of Adams/York counties, where Benjamin Franklin Frederick and the Mount Airy franchises are other Authority operators.
risk_flags: Out of PA core; ~73 mi from Lancaster

items.ownership_notes: Proud, family-owned local business since 1980; serves Elkton MD and Middletown DE.
items.strategic_rationale: Covers Cecil County MD and southern New Castle County DE, bridging Lancaster's southern edge (via US-1/Route 222) and the Delaware franchises.

items.ownership_notes: Locally owned; in business since 1984; headquartered in New Castle DE.
items.strategic_rationale: A New Castle County HVAC tuck-in that would add technicians to a Wilmington One Hour (Calvert's) combination.
risk_flags: Depends on first securing a Delaware anchor

items.ownership_notes: '& Sons' family firm; site says it has served the Mid-Atlantic for over 40 years with commercial and residential HVAC and plumbing.
items.strategic_rationale: A central Maryland scale option (112 employees) north of Baltimore and DC. It's only relevant if Punctual Pros pursues the Baltimore/Frederick corridor, where the Authority Brands Maryland franchises are clustered.

items.company: C&C Air Conditioning, Heating, Plumbing & Electric
items.ownership_notes: Founded 1965 by Charlie Baker; son Chris Sr. has led since 1995; third generation of Bakers now in the business; Lennox top dealer.
items.review_source: Company site: '4.9/5 Google Rating (2,000+ reviews)'; also 'over 1,200 five-star reviews'
items.strategic_rationale: The strongest Jersey Shore independent in the screen: a three-trade (HVAC/plumbing/electrical) business with ~65 employees, 2,000+ Google reviews at 4.9, and coverage of Monmouth, Middlesex, Somerset, Union and Essex. It extends Horvath north through Monmouth County along the Route 35/36 bayshore. A multi-generation family business with a third generation involved leaves an open succession question.
risk_flags: Third generation active, so the family may prefer to continue

items.revenue_source: ZoomInfo search_companies modeled estimate (retrieved 2026-09-24) (a second ZoomInfo record, Bovio & Rubino Service, Sicklerville, shows 17 emp/$3.64M)
items.ownership_notes: Family-owned and professionally operated since 1974; serving South Jersey for three generations; site cites 5,000+ 5-star reviews. The reported 2021 Bovio / Rubino Service combination is not confirmed on the company's About page.
items.strategic_rationale: South Jersey's review leader (5,000+ five-star reviews) with ~77 employees in Camden, Burlington and Gloucester counties. It fills the Philadelphia-to-Shore gap (One Hour Turnersville/Cherry Hill are separate franchisees) and brings insulation and energy-audit capability that fits One Hour's efficiency upsell.
risk_flags: 2021 merger means two founding families at the table
Sila (Allied Experts, Cherry Hill) is an active local competitor/acquirer

items.ownership_notes: Family-owned and proudly local since 2007 (Monroe/Helmetta).
items.strategic_rationale: A fast-growing ~71-employee operator in Monroe/South Middlesex, 32 miles north of Horvath's hub, that has grown to scale in under 20 years. It would give Punctual Pros Central Jersey mass between Toms River and the Somerset/Manalapan franchise territories.
risk_flags: Founder-growth mode (2007) may favor staying independent or taking a rival PE bid

items.ownership_notes: Family-owned since 1954; site explicitly contrasts itself with 'distant, out-of-town private equity firms'.
items.strategic_rationale: A 72-year-old Freehold HVAC brand 21 miles from Horvath, a density add in western Monmouth. Its anti-PE positioning means only an operator-led (Horvath) approach is likely to work.

items.ownership_notes: Family-owned residential HVAC since 1974 in Middlesex, Monmouth and Ocean counties; owner Christopher K. Madden; has a Toms River office.
items.strategic_rationale: Directly overlaps Horvath's Ocean/Monmouth footprint and already has a Toms River office. It's a pure route-density tuck-in for One Hour Toms River and Manalapan.

items.ownership_notes: 'The Shore Area's Finest Since 1990'; heating, cooling, plumbing and electrical.
items.strategic_rationale: A three-trade Monmouth shore operator (Asbury Park/Allenhurst). Its trade mix maps one-for-one onto Horvath's tri-brand along the northern Jersey Shore.

items.ownership_notes: Family business founded in 2002.
items.strategic_rationale: A Freehold plumbing tuck-in that adds Benjamin Franklin capacity in western Monmouth.

items.ownership_notes: Family owned and operated since 1911.
items.review_source: Company site Google widget: '4.9 Based on 1838 reviews'
items.strategic_rationale: A heavily reviewed Cape May County brand (1,838 at 4.9). It extends the South Jersey shore footprint next to the Pleasantville tri-brand franchise and suits second-home and seasonal service programs.
risk_flags: ~54 mi from Toms River; seasonal market

items.ownership_notes: Licensed, family-owned since 1949; three generations; Atlantic and Cape May counties.
items.strategic_rationale: Shares a town with the Pleasantville Authority tri-brand. It would be a density add-on if Punctual Pros enters Atlantic County through that franchise.
risk_flags: Value depends on first securing a South Jersey anchor

items.ownership_notes: Family owned and operated since 2001; NATE and EPA-certified technicians.
items.strategic_rationale: An Atlantic County HVAC add-on with ~25 employees. It would add One Hour capacity at the shore south of Toms River.

items.ownership_notes: Lenegan Plumbing Heating LLC, 200 West Ave, Ocean City NJ; NJ lic 9034.
items.strategic_rationale: An Ocean City shore plumbing/HVAC operator with ~29 employees and winterization and second-home service programs, which suit Benjamin Franklin shore routes.

items.ownership_notes: Founded 1945 by brothers Charles and Paul Laury; fourth generation of family leadership (Ted Laury; David Laury); Carrier President's Award.
items.strategic_rationale: A ~74-employee South Jersey anchor covering Atlantic, Camden, Cape May, Cumberland, Gloucester and Salem counties. It sits between Lancaster (across the Delaware Memorial Bridge) and the Jersey Shore franchises.

items.company: Harris Plumbing, Heating, Air & Electric (D.E. Harris Services Inc.)
items.revenue_source: ZoomInfo search_companies modeled estimate (retrieved 2026-09-24) (likely overstated; formerly included propane)
items.ownership_notes: Started as a chimney-cleaning company in 1986; formerly 'Harris Plumbing Heating Air & Propane'; licensed in NJ, PA and DE; 4.9 Google rating.
items.strategic_rationale: A founder-built, 172-employee, five-trade business licensed in NJ, DE and PA. From Salem NJ it reaches Wilmington and the Delaware Valley, making it the natural hinge between the Central PA and Jersey Shore footprints. The 1986 founding points to near-term succession.
risk_flags: ~55 mi from Lancaster and ~72 mi from Toms River; rural Salem County

items.ownership_notes: Licenses held by Peter R. Sanders (master plumber, master HVACR) with electrical licensee James J. Grasso; offices in Voorhees and Washington Twp NJ.
items.strategic_rationale: A ~101-employee, three-trade South Jersey operator (Camden/Gloucester) that could anchor a Philadelphia-to-Shore bridge next to One Hour and Mister Sparky Turnersville.
